sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in Gilbert, AZ?
sections.html:
A Gilbert owner can list with an agent, sell the house without an agent, or sell directly to a buyer who pays cash and takes the home as it stands. Each route trades time, effort and price in a different way. The right choice depends on the condition of the house, the date you need to close, and how much work you want to do before a buyer walks through the door.

  • Listing with an agent: the house is prepared, photographed and marketed, and the sale closes once the buyer's lender finishes its review.
  • Selling on your own: you set the price, run showings, handle disclosures and negotiate directly.
  • Selling for cash as-is: a buyer purchases the house in its current condition, which fits inherited homes, houses with deferred repairs, rentals with tenants in place, and owners working against a deadline.

Gilbert home values run high. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $575,100, against $332,700 for the country as a whole. At that level, a roof, an air conditioning unit or a kitchen update can cost real money, so many owners compare the net from a repaired listing with the net from a direct as-is sale before they decide.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the town of Gilbert?
sections.html:
Gilbert is a town in Maricopa County, southeast of Phoenix, with 287,285 residents on July 1, 2025 according to the Census Bureau. It sits south of Mesa, northeast of Chandler and northwest of Queen Creek, and it covers about 68.6 square miles of land. Gilbert is legally a town even though it is larger than most Arizona cities.

The place began in 1902 when William "Bobby" Gilbert provided land to the Arizona Eastern Railway for a line between Phoenix and Florence. Ayer's Grocery opened in 1910, the post office followed in 1912, and Gilbert incorporated on July 6, 1920. Hay shipping gave it the nickname "Hay Capital of the World" from 1911 until the late 1920s, and the 1913 Gilbert Elementary School building now houses the Gilbert Historical Museum. The population was 29,188 in 1990, 208,453 in 2010 and 267,918 in 2020.

Most Gilbert addresses are zoned to Gilbert Public Schools, while other parts of town fall in the Chandler Unified, Mesa Public Schools or Higley Unified districts. Buyers with children ask which district serves a house, so confirm it by address before you list. For commuting, the Santan Freeway portion of Loop 202 is the main freeway, US 60 touches the northern edge at the Higley Road interchange, and Phoenix Mesa Gateway Airport lies close by in east Mesa. Gilbert workers report a mean commute of 25.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Which Gilbert rules should a seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Start with the Town's Development Services office, which answers permit questions at (480) 503-6700 or onestopshop@gilbertaz.gov. Gilbert keeps extended customer hours of 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Thursday for most services, though building, engineering and fire inspections keep their own schedules. The Town currently works from its 2018 code amendments, and its draft reference for the 2024 code amendments is not adopted yet, with adoption listed for January 2027.

If you finished a patio, pool, garage conversion or accessory dwelling without a permit, ask Development Services what record exists before you sign a contract. The Town's permit page lists a residential fee calculator, an accessory dwelling unit guide, pool fence rules, a noise ordinance and a permit extension request form, and each one answers a question a buyer's inspector is likely to raise.

  • Short-term rental: the Town Council approved an ordinance in June 2023 that requires a Gilbert short-term rental license. The license and renewal fee is $250 as of October 1, 2026. Arizona law, A.R.S. 9-500.39, bars a town from banning short-term rentals outright but lets it require a permit, emergency contact details and liability coverage. Questions go to ShortTermRentals@gilbertaz.gov.
  • Long-term tenants: A.R.S. 33-1902 requires the owner of a rental house to keep registration details on file with the county assessor and to update them within ten days of a change.
  • HOA rules: if the house belongs to an association, its covenants can limit exterior changes, so gather those documents early.

sections.h2: What county paperwork does a Gilbert sale involve?
sections.html:
Every Gilbert deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder, and the recorder will refuse a deed that lacks a completed affidavit of value unless the deed shows an exemption on its face (A.R.S. 11-1133). Buyer and seller, or their agents, sign the affidavit together. It lists the parcel number, the sale date, the price and down payment, the financing type, whether personal property makes up 5% or more of the price, and whether the buyer will occupy the house or rent it.

Several transfers need no affidavit under A.R.S. 11-1134, and the deed must name the exemption it relies on.

  • A deed of gift.
  • A conveyance made under a court order.
  • A transfer for nominal consideration between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings.
  • A deed that only confirms or corrects an earlier recorded deed.

Recording costs $30 per instrument under A.R.S. 11-475, and that amount already includes the $2 real estate transfer fee in A.R.S. 11-1132. The Maricopa County Recorder's Office, reachable at 602-506-3535, states that it cannot give legal advice or help complete documents, so the title company or an attorney prepares the paperwork. Sales to a direct buyer normally run through the same escrow and title process as a listed sale.

sections.h2: How do Maricopa County property taxes affect a Gilbert sale?
sections.html:
Property tax on a Gilbert house is billed by Maricopa County, with half due October 1 and half due March 1. Under A.R.S. 42-18052, the first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. Maricopa's 2026 calendar shows November 2 as the first-half delinquency date, which has already passed. A bill of $100 or less is due October 1 and turns delinquent after December 31.

Ask the escrow officer how taxes will be prorated between you and the buyer, and make sure no unpaid half remains when you close. If you doubt the value the Assessor placed on the house, the appeal rules are short and strict.

  • The Assessor mails a Notice of Value between January 1 and March 1.
  • You have 60 days from the mailing date to file a petition for review, and the Assessor answers by August 15.
  • A denied petition can go to the State Board of Equalization within 25 days.
  • A court appeal is due by December 15 of the notice year, or within 60 days of the last administrative decision.
  • Only the full cash value can be appealed. Taxes are based on the limited property value, which generally cannot rise more than 5% a year.

sections.h2: What should a Gilbert owner gather before asking for offers?
sections.html:
A Gilbert owner should collect the parcel number, the latest tax bill, the HOA contact, a list of repairs and a record of permitted work before asking for offers. With these in hand, a buyer can price the house in one pass instead of coming back with follow-up questions. If the house is vacant, inherited or occupied by tenants, note that too, since each situation changes the closing steps.

Owners who want a fast result often ask a direct buyer for a written offer with the closing date and the net amount stated. Compare it against a listing price minus repairs, agent fees, holding costs and the weeks a house sits on the market. Read any purchase agreement fully, and have a title company or attorney review it before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need an affidavit of value to sell a house in Gilbert?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the transfer is exempt. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires buyer and seller to sign an affidavit that goes with the deed, and the Maricopa County Recorder refuses a deed without it unless an exemption such as a gift or a court-ordered conveyance is noted on the deed.

faqs.q: When are Gilbert property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. The first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, except that small bills of $100 or less are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. For 2026, Maricopa County lists November 2 as the first-half delinquency date.

Yes, with a Town license. Arizona law prevents a town from prohibiting short-term rentals, and Gilbert requires a license under its June 2023 ordinance. The license and renewal fee is $250 as of October 1, 2026, and ShortTermRentals@gilbertaz.gov handles questions.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Gilbert home's value?
faqs.a: You have 60 days from the date the Maricopa County Assessor mailed the Notice of Value. The petition goes to the Assessor first, and a denial can be taken to the State Board of Equalization within 25 days or to court by December 15.

faqs.q: Who records the deed after a Gilbert sale?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder records it, usually through the title or escrow company handling the closing. Recording is $30 per instrument, including the $2 transfer fee, and the office can be reached at 602-506-3535 for general questions.
